newsitem.title: UK: London Exchange disciplines number of AIM advisers.
newsitem.headline: London Exchange disciplines number of AIM advisers.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange said on Tuesday it was pursuing disciplinary action against a "small number" of nominated advisers involved in bringing companies to the Alternative Investment Market for fledgling companies.

Following a review of the performance of the 51 nominated advisers active in the AIM market, the Exchange said the majority provided high standards of professional practice but a number needed to strengthen procedures in certain areas.
It did not identify the firms in question but said they had been given directions on the improvements required.

"In a small number of cases, the Exchange found that practice was sufficiently unsatisfactory to warrant discplinary action," the Exchange said. "In these cases, further investigations and disciplinary procedures are being pursued."

The review is part of a continuing scrutiny by the Exchange of AIM, which has attracted 258 companies since its launch in 1995 but where the advisers involved in promoting stocks have a key role in what is intended as a more lax regulatory structure.
Designed for startup companies where the possibility of high gains counter the higher risk involved, the performance of some AIM stocks has nonetheless fallen short of some expectations.
The exchange said "almost all" AIM advisers "applied appropriate standards of diligence in bringing companies to AIM".
Yet one area singled out for improvement was the level of disclosure relating to shadow directors and promoters of companies coming to the market.

"Investor protection requires a full disclosure of all individuals who are instrumental in bringing a company to market," the Exchange said. "We shall continue to look for a high level of enquiry and disclosure in this area."

Advisers were urged to maintain adequate contact with their client companies and to ensure that profit projections were properly prepared and realistic and that announcements were made when targets were not going to be met.
The Exchange said it would continue the review of AIM advisers on a rolling basis.

"AIM has hade an excellent start. We shall build on this review to maintain the combination of quality regulation and accessibility which is necessary to protect investors and ensure the market's continued success," the Exchange said.
